text: Human beings have evolved. <break time="0.8s" /> To make the most of the resources available to them. <break time="0.8s" /> In ways that are subtle and complicated. <break time="0.8s" /> When we change our diets. <break time="0.8s" /> Especially when we do so quickly. <break time="0.8s" /> We are effectively conducting huge experiments in nutrition. <break time="0.8s" /> We ought to have more humility. <break time="0.8s" /> Nutritional science is still young. <break time="0.8s" /> And there is so much we do not know. <break time="0.8s" /> If we have eaten certain foods in certain ways. <break time="0.8s" /> For millennia. <break time="0.8s" /> We should assume. <break time="0.8s" /> Until it is proven otherwise. <break time="0.8s" /> That there is probably a good reason why. <break time="0.8s" /> Traditional foods that do not fit neatly on the contemporary dietary food plate. <break time="0.8s" /> Should generally be chosen. <break time="0.8s" /> Over highly processed ones that do. <break time="0.8s" /> We should assume. <break time="0.8s" /> That traditionally made fatty blood sausages. <break time="0.8s" /> Are preferable to lean, factory made salamis. <break time="0.8s" /> That spoonfuls of honey. <break time="0.8s" /> Are superior to sprinkles of sweeteners. <break time="0.8s" /> Witnessing how poorly traditional societies are faring. <break time="0.8s" /> As they undergo a nutrition transition. <break time="0.8s" /> Should make those who have already completed it. <break time="0.8s" /> Question whether their diets have moved too far.
